correctness.rationale: The root divisor identity (1-z)^d phi_d(2(1+z)/(1-z))=2(1+z^d) follows from the characteristic-p binomial formula for 2d=p^r+1. The geometric group mu_d semidirect C2 is a known primary theorem and is finite etale because p does not divide 2d. Over a finite field H^1(PGL2)=1, so forms equal twisted-conjugacy classes (a,epsilon) of finite dihedral cocycles, yielding the stated m_plus/m_minus counts. Fixed twisted conjugacy yields cyclic/dihedral arithmetic stabilizers; affine Frobenius j->epsilon*Q*j+a+(epsilon*Q-1)/2 yields all N_n and zeta products. Exact polynomial and group checks are reproducible in checker.py; finite checks do not establish the universal claim.

value.rationale: The exceptional Chebyshev root divisor is a distinguished finite-field Galois configuration with a large geometric symmetry group, but its arithmetic forms, descent of those symmetries and splitting cycles are not captured by the geometric theorem. A complete, uniform parametrization, all extension-field counts and explicit different zeta spectra distinguish actual arithmetical behavior in every odd characteristic and provide a reusable exact example of dihedral finite-field descent. The result is not merely a renamed stabilizer or a single small table.
